summary: Source decomposition of the rational relative period-sheaf theory of Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Sections 4 and 6 (with Lemma 3.18 and Lemma 5.5), read together with the 2013/2016 erratum: completed structure sheaves on the pro-etale site, affinoid perfectoid objects and their etale pullbacks, almost acyclicity of the completed integral structure sheaf, the sheaves A_inf, B_inf, B_dR^+, B_dR and their values on affinoid perfectoids, the corrected structural de Rham sheaf OB_dR^+ and its local description B_dR^+[[X_1, ..., X_n]], the Poincare lemma with Griffiths transversality and strict exactness, Faltings's extension, and the computation of the cohomology of gr^i OB_dR. This covers stage P8:local-rational and the B_dR^+ part of R06.1. The proper comparison suffix of P8, the period functors, monodromy, integral and geometric stages and the Robba-ring stage are recorded as not read.

nodes.title: A_inf, B_inf, B_dR^+ and B_dR of a perfectoid affinoid (K, K^+)-algebra; the element ξ
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 with an open bounded valuation subring K^+, and fix π ∈ K♭ with π♯/p ∈ (K^+)^×. For a perfectoid affinoid (K, K^+)-algebra (R, R^+) set A_inf(R, R^+) = W(R♭+), B_inf = A_inf[1/p], B_dR^+(R, R^+) = lim B_inf/(ker θ)^i. There is ξ ∈ A_inf(K, K^+) of the form ξ = [π] − Σ_{i≥1} p^i [x_i] (x_i ∈ O_{K♭}) generating ker(θ: A_inf(K, K^+) → K^+); ξ is not a zero-divisor, hence unique up to a unit, and for every (R, R^+) the same ξ generates ker(θ: A_inf(R, R^+) → R^+) and is a nonzerodivisor there. Consequently B_dR(R, R^+) := B_dR^+(R, R^+)[ξ^{-1}] carries the filtration Fil^i = ξ^i B_dR^+ with gr^i B_dR(R, R^+) ≅ ξ^i R, a free R-module of rank 1, and gr^• B_dR(R, R^+) ≅ R[ξ^{±1}].
hypotheses: K perfectoid of characteristic 0; π ∈ K♭ with |π♯| = |p| (π♯/p a unit of K^+); (R, R^+) perfectoid affinoid over (K, K^+), so R♭+ is flat over K♭+ and R^+ is flat over Z_p; θ: W(R♭+) → R^+ surjective (from PerfectoidSpaces P1).
The construction of ξ uses only that θ([π]) ∈ p(K^+)^× can be written as Σ_{i≥1} p^i θ([x_i]), i.e. surjectivity of θ for (K, K^+).
proofSteps: Nonzerodivisor: if ξ y = 0 with y = Σ p^i [y_i] ≠ 0, flatness of W(R♭+) over Z_p lets one assume y_0 ≠ 0; reducing mod p gives π y_0 = 0 in R♭+, impossible since R♭+ is flat over K♭+.

Generation: for y ∈ ker θ, W(R♭+)/(ξ, p) = R♭+/π = R^+/p shows y ≡ z_0 ξ mod p; iterating gives y − (Σ_{i≤k} p^i z_i) ξ ∈ p^{k+1} W(R♭+), and p-adic completeness and separatedness of W(R♭+) give y = (Σ p^i z_i) ξ.
Cor. 6.4: ξ has the same properties in B_inf, so gr^i B_dR(R, R^+) = ξ^i B_dR^+/ξ^{i+1} B_dR^+ ≅ ξ^i R.
acceptance: For (R, R^+) = (C, O_C), ξ generates ker θ ⊂ A_inf and B_dR^+(C) = lim A_inf[1/p]/ξ^i is the classical Fontaine ring with gr^i = C ξ^i.
The element t = log([ε]) ∈ Fil^1 B_dR^+(K, K^+), for K = completed Q_p(μ_{p^∞}), generates Fil^1 and Gal(Q_p(μ_{p^∞})/Q_p) acts on it through the cyclotomic character (used in Prop. 6.7).

sources.locator: Section 6, the definitions before Lemma 6.3, Lemma 6.3 with proof, Corollary 6.4 with proof, pp. 35-36 (extraction lines 2026-2081)
sources.excerpt: As a first step, we will find z_0 ∈ W(R♭+) so that y − z_0 ξ is divisible by p. Indeed, W(R♭+)/(ξ, p) = R♭+/π = R^+/p, so that f is mapped to zero in this quotient, which amounts to the existence of z_0 as desired.
sources.match: The principal-kernel argument, uniform in (R, R^+) over (K, K^+), which R06.1 needs for B_dR^+ and its filtration.

nodes.title: Structure sheaves O_X, O_X^+, Ô_X^+, Ô_X on X_proet and the continuous valuations on their sections
nodes.statement: For a locally noetherian adic space X over Spa(Q_p, Z_p), define on X_proet the uncompleted structure sheaf O_X = ν^* O_{X_et} with O_X^+ = ν^* O^+_{X_et}, the integral completed structure sheaf Ô_X^+ = lim O_X^+/p^n and Ô_X = Ô_X^+[1/p]. For U ∈ X_proet: every x ∈ |U| gives a continuous valuation f ↦ |f(x)| on O_X(U) which extends to Ô_X(U); O_X^+(U) = {f ∈ O_X(U) : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} and Ô_X^+(U) = {f ∈ Ô_X(U) : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}, so Ô_X^+(U) ⊂ Ô_X(U) is integrally closed; O_X^+/p^n → Ô_X^+/p^n is an isomorphism of sheaves and Ô_X^+(U) is flat over Z_p and p-adically complete.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian adic over Spa(Q_p, Z_p); U qcqs with a pro-etale presentation U = lim U_i (assertions are local in U).

The pro-etale site is Scholze's Definition 3.9 with the erratum's corrected notion of covers (transfinite compositions of pullbacks of finite etale surjections; unchanged for countable limits); the category X_proet itself is unchanged.

It is not known whether O_X(U) is dense in Ô_X(U) for arbitrary U, nor whether (|U|, Ô_X|_{|U|}, valuations) is always an adic space (remark after Lemma 4.2); both hold on the basis of affinoid perfectoid U.
proofSteps: (i) O_X(U) = colim O_X(U_i), and a point x is a compatible system of points x_i, so the valuations on O_X(U_i) combine.
(ii) For i large, |U| → |U_i| is surjective, so |f(x)| ≤ 1 on |U| forces |f_i(x_i)| ≤ 1 on |U_i| and f_i ∈ O_X^+(U_i).

(iii) formal from flatness of O_X^+ over Z_p; (iv) define |f(x)| via max(|f_n(x̃)|, |p|^n) over local lifts, which is independent of the lift; (v) reduce to: |f(x)| ≤ |p|^n everywhere implies f ∈ p^n Ô_X^+(U), by writing f = f_0 + p^n g on a cover and applying (ii) to f_0.
acceptance: For U = X affinoid, O_X(X) = O_{X_et}(X) and Ô_X^+(X) is the p-adic completion of O^+(X).
The valuations on Ô_X(U) are continuous for the topology with basis p^n Ô_X^+(U).

sources.locator: Section 4, Definition 4.1, Lemma 4.2 with proof and the following remark, pp. 21-22 (extraction lines 1134-1218)
sources.excerpt: We caution the reader that we do not know whether O_X(U) ⊂ Ô_X(U) is always dense with respect to the topology on Ô_X(U) having p^n Ô_X^+(U), n ≥ 0, as a basis of open neighborhoods of 0.

nodes.title: Affinoid perfectoid objects of X_proet, the functor U ↦ Û, and stability under etale and pro-etale maps
nodes.statement: Over a perfectoid field K of characteristic 0 with open bounded valuation subring K^+, and X locally noetherian over Spa(K, K^+): U ∈ X_proet is affinoid perfectoid if it has a pro-etale presentation U = lim U_i by affinoids U_i = Spa(R_i, R_i^+) such that, with R^+ the p-adic completion of colim R_i^+ and R = R^+[1/p], (R, R^+) is a perfectoid affinoid (K, K^+)-algebra; Û := Spa(R, R^+) is independent of the presentation, Û ~ lim U_i in the sense of Sch12 Definition 7.14 and |Û| = |U|. (Lemma 4.5) If V_i → U_i is etale, a composite of rational subsets and finite etale maps, then V = V_i ×_{U_i} U is affinoid perfectoid with V̂ = V_i ×_{U_i} Û and, for A_j the p-adic completion of the p-torsionfree quotient of S_j^+ ⊗_{R_j^+} R^+, S = A_j[1/p], the cokernel of A_j → S^+ is killed by a power of p, and for every ε > 0 in log Γ it is killed by p^ε for j large. (Lemma 4.6, Cor. 4.7) Anything pro-etale over a perfectoid U is perfectoid, and for X smooth over Spa(K, K^+) the affinoid perfectoid U form a basis of X_proet; Prop. 4.8 (Colmez) extends the basis statement to all locally noetherian X.
hypotheses: K perfectoid of characteristic 0 (needed so that perfectoid affinoid (K, K^+)-algebras make sense in Sch12's field-based framework); X locally noetherian over Spa(K, K^+).

Lemma 4.5 imports Sch12 Theorem 6.3(ii) (rational localizations of perfectoid affinoids are perfectoid), Lemma 6.4 (the subalgebras R^+⟨(f_i♯/g♯)^{1/p^m}⟩ with p^ε-bounded cokernel), Theorem 7.9(iii) (almost purity: S_j ⊗_{R_j} R perfectoid and uniformly almost finitely generated), Lemma 7.3(iv) and Proposition 7.10 (fibre products of finite etale maps).

Corollary 4.7 uses that a smooth X locally admits an etale map to the torus T^n (Huber [12] Corollary 1.6.10, unread) and the explicit cover T̃^n = lim Spa(K⟨T_i^{±1/p^m}⟩, K^+⟨T_i^{±1/p^m}⟩) of Example 4.4.
proofSteps: Rational case: W = pullback of the rational subset to Û has (T, T^+) = (O_Û(W), O^+_Û(W)) perfectoid affinoid; with the natural topology on T_j = S_j ⊗_{R_j} R making the image of S_j^+ ⊗ R^+ open and bounded, Spa(T_j, T_j^+) = V_j ×_{U_j} Û, and (T, T^+) is the completion of (T_j, T_j^+), so T = A_j[1/p] and T^+ bounded gives the p-power bound on the cokernel.
S^+ = T^+: injectivity of S_j^+/p^n → T^+/p^n for j large (W → V_j surjective) and surjectivity by approximating p^N f by elements of S_j^+ modulo p^{n+N} and dividing by p^N.
p^ε-bound: exhibit topologically finitely generated R^+-subalgebras T_ε^+ ⊂ T^+ with p^ε-torsion cokernel (Sch12 Lemma 6.4) and approximate their generators from S_j^+.

Finite etale case: T = S_j ⊗_{R_j} R is perfectoid by almost purity, Spa(T, T^+) is the fibre product by Sch12 7.3(iv)/7.10, and T^{+a} = T°a is uniformly almost finitely generated over R°a (7.9(iii)), giving the p^ε-bound.

Lemma 4.6: factor V → U as an inverse limit of finite etale surjections over an etale V_0 → U; each finite etale piece comes from a finite level and completed direct limits of perfectoid affinoids are perfectoid affinoid.
acceptance: T̃^n ∈ (T^n)_proet is affinoid perfectoid with (T̃^n)^ = Spa(K⟨T_i^{±1/p^∞}⟩, K^+⟨T_i^{±1/p^∞}⟩).
For a rational subset {|T| ≤ |p|} of the torus, the cokernel of A_j → S^+ is p-power torsion but not zero at any finite level j.

sources.locator: Section 4, Definition 4.3, Example 4.4, Lemma 4.5 with proof, Lemma 4.6, Corollary 4.7, Proposition 4.8 (statement), pp. 22-25 (extraction lines 1219-1377)
sources.excerpt: Then (T, T^+) is a perfectoid affinoid (K, K^+)-algebra by Theorem 6.3 (ii) of [18], W = Spa(T, T^+). Recall that for perfectoid affinoid (K, K^+)-algebras (A, A^+), A^+ is open and bounded, i.e. carries the p-adic topology.
sources.match: Shows exactly where the PerfectoidSpaces sheaf theorem and boundedness enter the pullback lemma.

nodes.title: Ô_X^+(U) = R^+ and almost vanishing of H^i(U, Ô_X^+) for affinoid perfectoid U
nodes.statement: Let U ∈ X_proet be affinoid perfectoid with Û = Spa(R, R^+), in the almost setting for K^+ and its ideal of topologically nilpotent elements. Then (i) O_X^+(U)/b = R^+/b for nonzero b ∈ K^+, and this is almost equal to (O_X^+/b)(U); (ii) the image of (O_X^+/b_1)(U) in (O_X^+/b_2)(U) equals R^+/b_2 when |b_1| < |b_2|; (iii) Ô_X^+(U) = R^+ and Ô_X(U) = R; (iv) Ô_X^+(U) is the p-adic completion of O_X^+(U); (v) H^i(U, Ô_X^+) is almost zero for i > 0. In particular for perfectoid U, (|U|, Ô_X|_{|U|}, valuations) is the perfectoid space Û. (Lemma 3.18) If for an inverse system F_i of abelian sheaves there is a basis B with R^1 lim F_i(U) = 0 and H^j(U, F_i) = 0 (j > 0) for U ∈ B, then R^j lim F_i = 0 for j > 0, (lim F_i)(U) = lim F_i(U), and H^j(U, lim F_i) = 0 for U ∈ B, j > 0.
hypotheses: U affinoid perfectoid; covers of U may be assumed to be a single V = lim V_j → V_{j'} → U with V_{j'} a composite of rational embeddings and finite etale maps and V_j → V_{j'} finite etale surjective (uses the corrected covering notion and quasicompactness of U).

Imports: giving a sheaf on X_proet is equivalent to giving a presheaf on affinoid perfectoid objects with the sheaf property for pro-etale covers by such (Proposition 4.8/Corollary 4.7); Lemma 4.5 (Čech complex of the cover is that of the etale cover V̂ → Û); Sch12 Proposition 7.13 (H^i(W_et, O^{+a}_W) = 0 for affinoid perfectoid W); the almost version of Lemma 3.18.
proofSteps: (i) F(U) := (O^+(Û)/b)^a is a sheaf with vanishing higher cohomology: reduce the Čech complex of a cover V → U to a direct limit of Čech complexes of etale covers V̂_j → Û, which are almost exact by Sch12 7.13; hence F = (O_X^+/b)^a.
(ii) For f ∈ (O_X^+/b_1)(U) and c = b_1/b_2, c f = g comes from R^+ by (i); by valuations g = c h with h ∈ R^+, and injectivity of c: O_X^+/b_2 → O_X^+/b_1 gives f ≡ h in (O_X^+/b_2)(U).
(iii) Ô_X^+(U) = lim (O_X^+/p^n)(U) = lim R^+/p^n = R^+ by (ii); invert p for Ô_X(U) = R.

(v) H^i(U, O_X^+/p^n) almost zero for all n by (i); conclude with the almost version of Lemma 3.18 (R^1 lim vanishes on the basis because the transition maps on sections are surjective up to almost zero).
acceptance: For U = T̃^n, Ô_X(U) = K⟨T_i^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and H^i(U, Ô_X^+) is almost zero for i > 0.
The statement is 'almost equal' in (i) and 'equal' in (iii): passing to the inverse limit over n removes the almost defect using (ii).

sources.locator: Section 4, Lemma 4.10 with proof and Remark 4.11, pp. 26-27 (extraction lines 1426-1503); Lemma 3.18 with proof, pp. 20-21 (extraction lines 1093-1133)
sources.excerpt: so the statement follows from the vanishing of H^i(W_et, O^{+a}_{W_et}), i > 0, for any affinoid perfectoid space W, proved in [18], Proposition 7.13. This shows in particular that F = (O_X^+/b)^a, giving part (i).
sources.match: The reduction of pro-etale almost acyclicity to the etale almost acyclicity of PerfectoidSpaces P3.

nodes.title: The pro-etale period sheaves A_inf, B_inf, B_dR^+, B_dR and their filtrations
nodes.statement: On X_proet for X locally noetherian over Spa(Q_p, Z_p): A_inf = W(Ô^+_{X♭}) with B_inf = A_inf[1/p] and θ: A_inf → Ô_X^+ extending to θ: B_inf → Ô_X; B_dR^+ = lim B_inf/(ker θ)^n with Fil^i B_dR^+ = (ker θ)^i B_dR^+; B_dR = B_dR^+[t^{-1}] for any local generator t of Fil^1 B_dR^+, with Fil^i B_dR = Σ_{j∈Z} t^{-j} Fil^{i+j} B_dR^+. Locally on X_proet the element t exists, is unique up to a unit and is not a zero-divisor, so B_dR and its filtration are well defined.
hypotheses: Ô^+_{X♭} is the tilted completed integral structure sheaf (Definition 5.9 of the source, not read here; it is lim_Φ Ô_X^+/p on affinoid perfectoids); the Witt vector sheaf is taken sectionwise.
Existence, uniqueness and regularity of t are proved locally by Theorem 6.5(i) on affinoid perfectoid U (see the next node); before that the definition of B_dR is only provisional.
proofSteps: Sheaves are defined by the displayed formulas; the inverse limit defining B_dR^+ is taken in sheaves.
acceptance: On an affinoid perfectoid U with Û = Spa(R, R^+) these sheaves have sections A_inf(R, R^+), B_inf(R, R^+), B_dR^+(R, R^+), B_dR(R, R^+) (Theorem 6.5).
gr^i B_dR ≅ Ô_X(i) globally on X_proet (Proposition 6.7).

sources.locator: Section 6, Definition 6.1 and Remark 6.2, p. 35 (extraction lines 2006-2024)
sources.excerpt: We will see that locally on X_proet, the element t exists, is unique up to a unit and is not a zero-divisor. This shows that the sheaf B_dR and its filtration are well-defined.
sources.match: The definition and the deferred well-definedness claim.

nodes.title: Values and acyclicity of the period sheaves on affinoid perfectoids; profinite covers; gr^i B_dR = Ô_X(i)
nodes.statement: Let X be locally noetherian over Spa(K, K^+), K perfectoid of characteristic 0, and U ∈ X_proet affinoid perfectoid with Û = Spa(R, R^+). (Theorem 6.5) (i) A_inf(U) = A_inf(R, R^+), and likewise for B_inf, B_dR^+, B_dR; in particular ξ generates Fil^1 B_dR^+(U), is unique up to a unit and is not a zero-divisor. (ii) H^i(U, F) is almost zero for i > 0 for each of these sheaves (almost setting relative to A_inf(K, K^+) and the ideal generated by all [π^{1/p^N}]). (iii) [π] is invertible in B_dR^+(U) and B_dR(U), so their higher cohomology vanishes outright. (Corollary 6.6) For a profinite set S and V = U × S, F(V) = Hom_cont(S, F(U)) for F among Ô_X^+, Ô_X, Ô^+_{X♭}, Ô_{X♭}, A_inf, B_inf, B_dR^+, B_dR, gr^i B_dR, with the natural inverse/direct limit and quotient topologies. (Proposition 6.7) gr^i B_dR ≅ Ô_X(i) on X_proet, where (i) is the Tate twist by Ẑ_p(1) = lim μ_{p^n}.
hypotheses: Theorem 6.5 relies on the description of W(Ô^+_{X♭})/p^m by induction on m with almost vanishing, Lemma 3.18 for the inverse limit, exactness of the direct limit for B_inf, and the exact sequences 0 → B_inf → B_inf → B_inf/(ker θ)^i → 0 whose defect on sections is controlled by the almost zero H^1(U, B_inf).
The step from 'almost zero' to 'zero' for B_dR^+ and B_dR uses that [π] maps to the unit π♯ in B_inf(K, K^+)/(ker θ) = K, so [π] is invertible in B_inf/(ker θ), hence in B_dR^+.

Proposition 6.7 uses K = completed Q_p(μ_{p^∞}), t = log([ε]) with the Galois group acting through the cyclotomic character, and Proposition 3.15 (X_{K,proet} ≅ X_proet/X_K, not read) to descend from X_K to X.
proofSteps: Describe W(Ô^+_{X♭})/p^m on U inductively (each graded piece is Ô^+_{X♭}, whose sections and almost acyclicity come from the tilted version of Lemma 4.10); apply Lemma 3.18 for A_inf, then a direct limit for B_inf.

For B_dR^+: exactness of 0 → B_inf(U) → B_inf(U) → (B_inf/(ker θ)^i)(U) → 0 up to the almost zero H^1(U, B_inf); invertibility of [π] in B_inf/(ker θ) upgrades almost statements to actual ones; pass to the inverse limit.
Corollary 6.6: 'go through all identifications' (the source gives no further argument).
Proposition 6.7: over X_{K,proet}, gr^i B_dR = t^i Ô_X with t = log([ε]) generating Fil^1; the cyclotomic action descends the isomorphism to gr^i B_dR ≅ Ô_X(i).
acceptance: For U = X̃_K (the perfectoid torus cover) and S = Z_p^n, the Čech nerve of X̃_K → X_K has terms X̃_K × Z_p^{n(j-1)}, so the Cartan-Leray spectral sequence computes continuous group cohomology (used in Prop. 6.16).
B_dR^+(U) = B_dR^+(R, R^+) carries the ξ-adic filtration with gr^i = ξ^i R.

sources.locator: Section 6, Theorem 6.5 with proof, Corollary 6.6, Proposition 6.7 with proof, pp. 36-37 (extraction lines 2082-2142)
sources.excerpt: We see that all statements follow once we know that [π] is invertible in B_inf/(ker θ). But the latter is a sheaf of B_inf(K, K^+)/(ker θ) = K-modules, and [π] maps to the unit π♯ ∈ K^×.
sources.match: The mechanism converting almost acyclicity into actual acyclicity for the rational period sheaves, which the stage's 'rational local acyclicity' refers to.

nodes.title: The structural de Rham sheaves OB_dR^+ and OB_dR (corrected definition) and their connection
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k a discretely valued complete extension of Q_p with perfect residue field κ. Ω^1_X = ν^* Ω^1_{X_et}. Corrected definition (erratum item (3)): for affinoid perfectoid U = lim U_i, U_i = Spa(R_i, R_i^+), with completed direct limit (R, R^+), OB_dR^+ is the sheafification of the presheaf U ↦ colim_i of the ker θ-adic completion of (R_i^+ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} A_inf(R, R^+))[1/p], where ⊗̂ is the p-adic completion of the tensor product and θ is the tensor product of R_i^+ → R^+ with θ: A_inf(R, R^+) → R^+. Fil^i OB_dR^+ = (ker θ)^i OB_dR^+, OB_dR = OB_dR^+[t^{-1}] with Fil^i OB_dR = Σ_j t^{-j} Fil^{i+j} OB_dR^+. The original definition OB_dR^+ = lim (O_X ⊗_{W(κ)} B_inf)/(ker θ)^n (Definition 6.8) is wrong. OB_inf = O_X ⊗_{W(κ)} B_inf carries a unique B_inf-linear connection ∇ extending that of O_X, which extends B_dR^+-linearly to OB_dR^+ and B_dR-linearly to OB_dR.
hypotheses: X smooth over a discretely valued k with perfect residue field (needed for W(κ) and for the local etale maps to tori); the sheaves live on X_proet.

The erratum states that with the corrected definition 'the results of the paper are not affected'; the extension of ∇ to the corrected completion is asserted in Remark 6.9 for the original definition and must be re-checked for the corrected one (the erratum does not discuss ∇ explicitly; see gap).
proofSteps: Definition; the connection on OB_inf is the tensor product connection d ⊗ 1 and extends to completions by continuity.
acceptance: On U ∈ X_proet/X̃ affinoid perfectoid, OB_dR^+(U) = B_dR^+(R, R^+)[[X_1, ..., X_n]] (erratum's strengthened Proposition 6.10), which is already a sheaf on X_proet/X̃.
gr^0 OB_dR restricted to X_proet/X̃_K is Ô_X[X_1/ξ, ..., X_n/ξ] (Corollary 6.15).

sources.excerpt: Then OB_dR^+ is the sheafification of the presheaf sending U to the direct limit over i of the ker θ-adic completion of (R_i^+ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} A_inf(R, R^+))[1/p]. Here, the completed tensor product is the p-adic completion of the tensor product
sources.match: The corrected construction required verbatim by the stage text ('p-adically completed tensor with A_inf before p-inversion and kernel-of-theta completion, followed by the specified colimit/sheafification').

sources.locator: Section 6, Definition 6.8 and Remark 6.9, p. 37 (extraction lines 2143-2175)

nodes.title: OB_dR^+|_X̃ ≅ B_dR^+|_X̃[[X_1, ..., X_n]] over an etale map to the torus
nodes.statement: Let X → T^n be etale, X̃ = X ×_{T^n} T̃^n, and u_i = T_i ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ [T_i♭] ∈ OB_inf|_X̃ (in ker θ). Then X_i ↦ u_i defines an isomorphism B_dR^+|_X̃[[X_1, ..., X_n]] → OB_dR^+|_X̃ of sheaves on X_proet/X̃. Strengthened form (erratum): for U ∈ X_proet/X̃_K affinoid perfectoid with (R, R^+) as above and i sufficiently large, the ker θ-adic completion S_i of (R_i^+ ⊗̂_{W(κ)} A_inf(R, R^+))[1/p] is isomorphic to B_dR^+(R, R^+)[[X_1, ..., X_n]] via the constructed map, independently of i, so OB_dR^+(U) = B_dR^+(R, R^+)[[X_1, ..., X_n]].
hypotheses: X smooth over Spa(k, O_k) with an etale map to T^n; K a perfectoid completion of an algebraic extension of k; work over X_proet/X̃_K.

Lemma 6.11: for a finitely generated O_k-algebra S, any f: S → B_dR^+(R, R^+)[[X]] with θ(f(S)) ⊂ R^+ extends to the p-adic completion of S (because finitely generated R^+-submodules of gr^i B_dR^+(R, R^+) ≅ R are p-adically complete).

Lemma 6.12: an affinoid U = Spa(R, R^+) of finite type over Spa(W(κ)[1/p], W(κ)) with an etale map to T^n has R^+ = p-adic completion of a finitely generated W(κ)[T^{±1}]-algebra R_0^+ with R_0 = R_0^+[1/p] etale over W(κ)[1/p][T^{±1}]; this uses Huber [12] Corollary 1.7.3(iii), Remark 1.2.6(iii) and excellence of W(κ) (unread).
Hensel's lemma for the ker θ-adically complete ring B_dR^+(U)[[X]] with residue ring Ô_X(U).
proofSteps: Construct W(κ)[1/p][T^{±1}] → B_dR^+|_X̃[[X]] by T_i ↦ [T_i♭] + X_i (invertible since its reduction [T_i♭] is).

For affinoid perfectoid U = lim U_i over X̃_K, apply Lemma 6.12 to U_i → T^n, lift the etale algebras R_{i0} uniquely by Hensel's lemma to B_dR^+(U)[[X]], extend to the p-adic completions R_i^+ by Lemma 6.11, and take direct limits: this gives an O_X|_X̃_K-algebra structure on B_dR^+|_X̃_K[[X]] compatible with the reduction B_dR^+[[X]]/(ker θ) = Ô_X and sending T_i to [T_i♭] + X_i.
This induces (O_X ⊗_{W(κ)} W(Ô^+_{X♭}))|_X̃_K → B_dR^+|_X̃_K[[X]] and hence OB_dR^+|_X̃_K → B_dR^+|_X̃_K[[X]], inverse to X_i ↦ u_i.

Erratum: the composite S_i → B_dR^+(R, R^+)[[X]] → S_i is the identity because (B_dR^+(R, R^+)/ξ^r)[X]/(X)^r → (R_i^+ ⊗̂ A_inf(R, R^+))[1/p]/(ker θ)^r is surjective for each r: R_i^+[X]/(X)^r → (R_i^+ ⊗̂ R_i^+)/(ker θ_i)^r is injective with p-power-torsion cokernel, base change along R_i^+ → (B_dR(R, R^+)/ξ^r)_0 (an open bounded subring) gives an isomorphism up to bounded p-power torsion, and inverting p and using (ker θ_i)^r ⊗̂ (B_dR/ξ^r)_0 ⊂ (ker θ)^r concludes.
acceptance: For X = T^n itself, OB_dR^+(X̃_K) = B_dR^+(R̃, R̃^+)[[X_1, ..., X_n]] with (R̃, R̃^+) the perfectoid torus algebra, and u_i = T_i − [T_i♭].
The erratum notes that 'the analogue of this assertion fails with the original definition of OB_dR^+', i.e. the corrected completion is necessary for S_i → B_dR^+[[X]] → S_i to be the identity.

nodes.title: The relative Poincare lemma, Griffiths transversality, strict exactness, Faltings's extension and gr^• OB_dR
nodes.statement: For X smooth of dimension n over Spa(k, O_k), the sequence 0 → B_dR^+ → OB_dR^+ → OB_dR^+ ⊗_{O_X} Ω^1_X → ... → OB_dR^+ ⊗_{O_X} Ω^n_X → 0 of sheaves on X_proet is exact; ∇ satisfies Griffiths transversality ∇(Fil^i) ⊂ Fil^{i-1} ⊗ Ω^1, and with Ω^i_X in degree i the sequence is strict exact for the filtrations. Consequently (Faltings's extension) 0 → Ô_X(1) → gr^1 OB_dR^+ → Ô_X ⊗_{O_X} Ω^1_X → 0 is exact, and over X_proet/X̃_K, gr^i OB_dR ≅ ξ^i Ô_X[X_1/ξ, ..., X_n/ξ], so gr^• OB_dR ≅ Ô_X[ξ^{±1}, X_1, ..., X_n] with ξ and X_i in degree 1.
hypotheses: X smooth over Spa(k, O_k), k discretely valued with perfect residue field; the statements are local on X_proet and are checked on X_proet/X̃ using the local description B_dR^+[[X_1, ..., X_n]].

Sch13 proves the Poincare lemma by 'Using the description of Proposition 6.10, this is obvious': the de Rham complex of B_dR^+[[X_1, ..., X_n]] over B_dR^+ with ∇(X_i) = dT_i... (formal power series Poincare lemma in characteristic 0); the identification of ∇ under Proposition 6.10 (∇ u_i = dT_i) is used implicitly.
proofSteps: Under Proposition 6.10, OB_dR^+|_X̃ is the formal power series ring over B_dR^+|_X̃ in the u_i with ∇(u_i) = dT_i ⊗ 1; the de Rham complex of a power series ring over a Q-algebra is a resolution of the constants, and the filtration statements are read off degreewise.
Faltings's extension is the first graded piece of the strict exact Poincare sequence, using gr^1 B_dR^+ = Ô_X(1) (Proposition 6.7).
Corollary 6.15: gr^i of B_dR^+[[X]] with the (ξ, X_1, ..., X_n)-adic filtration is ξ^i Ô_X[X_1/ξ, ..., X_n/ξ].
acceptance: R^1 ν_* Ô_X(1) ≅ Ω^1_{X_et} via the connecting map of Faltings's extension (Corollary 6.19).
For n = 0 the Poincare lemma reads B_dR^+ = OB_dR^+.

nodes.title: Cohomology of gr^i OB_dR on affinoids with a toric etale chart; ν_* OB_dR = O_{X_et} and R^1 ν_* Ô_X(1) = Ω^1
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(R, R^+) be affinoid of finite type over Spa(k, O_k) with an etale map X → T^n which is a composite of rational embeddings and finite etale maps. (i) If K contains all p-power roots of unity, H^q(X_K, gr^0 OB_dR) = 0 for q > 0 and equals R ⊗̂_k K for q = 0. (ii) H^q(X, gr^i OB_dR) = 0 unless i = 0 and q ∈ {0, 1}; (gr^0 OB_dR)(X) = R and H^1(X, gr^0 OB_dR) = R · log χ, χ the cyclotomic character. Consequently, for X smooth over Spa(k, O_k): ν_* OB_dR = O_{X_et}, ν_* Ô_X = O_{X_et}, ν_* Ô_X(n) = 0 for n ≥ 1, R^1 ν_* Ô_X(1) ≅ Ω^1_{X_et} via the connecting map of Faltings's extension, R^1 ν_* Ô_X(n) = 0 for n ≥ 2; more generally R^i ν_* Ô_X(j) = Ω^i_{X_et} for i = j, Ω^i_{X_et} log χ for i = j + 1, and 0 otherwise.
hypotheses: X affinoid of finite type over Spa(k, O_k) with the stated toric etale chart; K = completion of k(μ_{p^∞}) in (ii), Γ_k = Gal(k(μ_{p^∞})/k).

Inputs: Cartan-Leray for the Z_p^n-cover X̃_K → X_K whose fibre products are affinoid perfectoid (so the higher cohomology of the sheaves vanishes there); Corollary 6.6 for gr^0 OB_dR; Lemma 6.17 (γ_i(V_j) = V_j + δ_{ij} for V_i = t^{-1} log([T_i♭]/T_i)); Lemma 6.18 (R^+ ⊗̂_{O_k⟨T^{±1}⟩} O_K⟨T^{±1/p^∞}⟩ → R̃^+ injective with p-power-torsion cokernel, from Lemma 4.5(ii)); Lemma 5.5 (continuous Z_p^n-cohomology of the perfectoid torus via the Koszul complex, with the cokernel of ∧^q R_0^n → H^q_cont(Z_p^n, R) killed by ζ_p − 1 and compatibility with base change); Brinon [5] Proposition 4.1.2 (unread); Tate's computation of H^q_cont(Γ_k, Q_p(i)) ([19], unread).
proofSteps: (i) H^q(X_K, gr^0 OB_dR) = H^q_cont(Z_p^n, gr^0 OB_dR(X̃_K)) with gr^0 OB_dR(X̃_K) = R̃[V_1, ..., V_n]; the inclusion (R ⊗̂_k K)[V] ⊂ R̃[V] induces an isomorphism on continuous cohomology (check on the associated graded for the polynomial degree, where Z_p^n acts trivially on the V_i, and use Lemma 6.18 with Lemma 5.5 for R ⊗̂ K ⊂ R̃).
Compute H^q_cont(Z_p^n, (R ⊗̂ K)[V]) inductively: γ_i − 1 acts on S[V_i] by P ↦ P(V_i + 1) − P(V_i), with kernel the constants and trivial cokernel.

(ii) All gr^i OB_dR are isomorphic to gr^0 on X_proet/X_K; for the cover X_K → X with Γ_k-fibre products, H^q(X_K^{m/X}, gr^i OB_dR) = Hom_cont(Γ_k^{m-1}, H^q(X_K, gr^i OB_dR)), giving H^q(X, gr^i OB_dR) = H^q_cont(Γ_k, R ⊗̂_k K(i)) = R ⊗_{Q_p} H^q_cont(Γ_k, Q_p(i)) (the map R(i) → R ⊗̂ K(i) is a Γ_k-cohomology isomorphism as in Lemma 5.5), and Tate's computation of the latter.

Corollary 6.19: after inverting t the Poincare lemma gives 0 → B_dR → OB_dR → ..., whose 0-th graded piece injects ν_* Ô_X into ν_* gr^0 OB_dR = O_{X_et}; the graded pieces 0 → Ô_X(n) → gr^n OB_dR → gr^{n-1} OB_dR ⊗ Ω^1 → ... give the vanishing and the identification of R^1 ν_* Ô_X(1).
acceptance: For X = T^n over k, H^1(X, gr^0 OB_dR) = k⟨T^{±1}⟩ log χ and R^1 ν_* Ô_X(1) = Ω^1 with basis dT_i/T_i.
The result H^q(X, gr^i OB_dR) = 0 for i ≠ 0 is what makes the de Rham comparison (Section 7 of the source) work; it is not proved here for non-toric charts.
